newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian pyramid boss's wife offers cash for votes.
newsitem.headline: Russian pyramid boss's wife offers cash for votes.

text.p: Yelena Mavrodi, wife of the organiser of a pyramid investment scheme which swallowed the savings of millions of Russians in 1994, launched a cash-for-votes bid on Friday to help win a seat in parliament.

Mavrodi, whose husband Sergei is still free to operate a new get-rich-quick scheme despite the collapse of MMM, is running for the State Duma seat in Tula, south of Moscow, which was vacated by sacked Security Council secretary Alexander Lebed.

Itar-Tass news agency said Yelena, a model, signed agreements with several dozen local folk, paying them 3,000 roubles ($0.55) and offering them "up to 50 million roubles ($9,000) according to voting results in their wards" on polling day, February 9.

Those who signed up as "activists" were also given blank forms to attract others into the scheme, Tass said, although the agreements did not specify the scale of the rewards nor commit the activists to actually voting for the candidate themselves.
"Another pyramid has come out of the election campaigning," Tass quoted local politician Nikolai Matveyev as saying.
Mavrodi has stood for the Duma before, coming third in a by-election near Moscow in May 1995.

She was following in her husband's footsteps. Shortly after spending two months in custody following the collapse of MMM, he was elected to the Duma, thus winning immunity from prosecution. But he was ejected by his peers a year later, in autumn 1995.

The Mavrodis have consistently argued they and those who lost money in the collapse of their scheme -- which relied on an ever-growing number of savers to produce 3,000 percent interest -- were the victims of state persecution.

The Tula by-election was made necessary when Lebed quit to join the Kremlin staff last summer -- he was sacked by President Boris Yeltsin in October. It has attracted a host of colourful candidates, including Yeltsin's dismissed former bodyguard Alexander Korzhakov, who has Lebed's personal backing.
Also planning to stand is chess grandmaster Anatoly Karpov.
